Summary: SupportWave is a fast-growing contact center SaaS that runs managed BPO operations for retail + telco clients. Primary ask = 24/7 dedicated capacity for multi-tenant agent-assist and automated ticketing pipelines. They need predictable latency during Black Friday-style spikes and isolation for customer data.

Recent conversations: 
- 2026-02-26 discovery call (Jordan + Priya) — very interested in Dedicated; mentioned existing latency complaints with current provider during peak windows. 
- 2026-03-03 technical deep-dive (Priya + infra lead Mateo) — asked about KV cache behavior across sessions, prefix caching, and failover model for model-variant fallback. See Fireflies ff_20260303_supportwave_call_8123.

Requirements / signals: 
- Workload: mix of short synchronous agent-assist calls (median response target <150ms p95) + async ticket summarization and triage (batch embeddings + reranking).
- Throughput target: steady-state 600–1,000 concurrent agent sessions, peak bursts to 3,000 concurrent during promotions.
- Latency SLOs: agent-assist p95 <= 200ms, tail handling for spikes with automated fallback to smaller model variant.
- Isolation: reserved GPU pools, VPC peering, no co-tenancy for production tenants (must be dedicated).
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, audit logs retained 1 year.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit cost < current provider by ~20% and if fallbacks preserve UX.

- "We cannot have agents waiting more than a second for suggestions — that kills CSAT." — Head of Ops, SupportWave.
